field.label: Enable
field.help: Enable the openvpn-auth-oauth2 SSO service.

field.label: OpenVPN instance
field.help: The OpenVPN server instance to protect with SSO. Leave that instance's Authentication field empty; the required SSO directives are kept on the instance automatically, and an instance that runs without 'management-client-auth' is stopped (see Advanced).

field.label: Tenant ID
field.help: Entra ID directory (tenant) GUID or tenant domain; used to derive the issuer URL.

field.label: Custom issuer URL
field.help: Overrides the issuer derived from the tenant ID. Leave empty for Entra ID; set to connect a different OIDC provider (e.g. https://idp.example.com).

field.label: Client ID
field.help: Application (client) ID of the app registration. For Entra ID this is a GUID; other OIDC providers may use any identifier.

field.label: Client secret
field.help: Client secret of the app registration. Leave empty for a public client (PKCE). Note the expiry date: Entra secrets are valid for at most 24 months.

field.label: Scopes
field.help: Space-separated OIDC scopes requested from the provider.

field.label: Allowed groups
field.help: Entra ID group object IDs allowed to connect. Empty allows every authenticated user.

field.label: Match IP address
field.help: Require the browser session and the VPN client to come from the same IP address. Breaks logins when browser and VPN client take different network paths (e.g. CGNAT).

field.label: Pending-auth timeout (s)
field.help: How long a client may take to finish the browser login.

field.label: Public base URL
field.help: URL the user's browser reaches the firewall on, e.g. https://vpn.example.nl:9443; it must match DNS and the certificate, and be registered as redirect URI base in Entra.

field.label: Listen address
field.help: Local IPv4 or IPv6 address the callback listener binds to.

field.label: Listen port
field.help: TCP port of the callback listener; remember the matching firewall rule and the redirect URI registered in Entra. Do not use 9000: the web GUI's PHP backend already listens there.

field.label: Encryption secret
field.help: Random secret of exactly 16, 24 or 32 alphanumeric characters. Click the gear button next to this label to generate one on the firewall with openssl rand -hex 16 (32 characters), then click Save to store it. Encrypts the browser state cookies and stored refresh tokens.

field.label: Enable TLS
field.help: Serve the callback listener over HTTPS (required by several VPN clients).

field.label: Certificate
field.help: Server certificate from the OPNsense trust store for the HTTPS listener.

field.label: Logo
field.help: Optional. Shown at the top of the page the browser displays after sign-in. PNG, JPEG, SVG or WebP, up to 64 KB.

field.label: Repair OpenVPN instance directives
field.help: Keep 'management-client-auth', 'auth-user-pass-optional' and 'auth-gen-token ... external-auth' on the selected instance. The instance's Options field cannot show these directives and drops them whenever the instance is saved in VPN > OpenVPN > Instances. With this option on they are written back within a few seconds, and again right before every Apply there, at boot and on CARP events, so the instance is not restarted for it. If the instance is ever found running without 'management-client-auth', the SSO guard stops it at once (dropping its tunnels) and, with this option on, restores the directives and starts it again. With this option off nothing is written into the instance, and the guard keeps such an instance stopped. Protection cannot be switched off while SSO is enabled.

field.label: Auth token lifetime (s)
field.help: How long a client may stay connected since its browser sign-in before it must sign in again. OpenVPN counts this from the first sign-in and the hourly renewals do not extend it; at the first renegotiation past it the session is refused and the client reconnects with a browser prompt, which on a full-tunnel profile only works with 'persist-tun' removed (see Client profile). The daemon re-checks the session with the identity provider at every renegotiation regardless, so a long lifetime costs little. Injected into the instance as 'auth-gen-token ... external-auth' by the repair above; the instance's own Auth Token Lifetime field must stay empty, otherwise the injection is skipped to avoid a duplicate directive.

field.label: GUI status pass-through
field.help: Keep VPN > OpenVPN > Connection Status working by proxying the management socket. Disable ("exclusive mode") only if the socket swap misbehaves.

field.label: Log level
field.help: Verbosity of the daemon log.

field.label: Remove persist-tun
field.help: Applied by the export type 'File Only (SSO, openvpn-auth-oauth2)' on VPN > OpenVPN > Client Export. With 'persist-tun' the client keeps the tunnel adapter and its routes across a reconnect; when that reconnect needs a browser sign-in, a full-tunnel client has its default route in a tunnel that carries nothing yet, cannot reach the identity provider, and stays stuck until it is disconnected by hand. Without it the routes are removed on reconnect and the sign-in page loads over the normal connection.

field.label: Remove persist-key
field.help: OpenVPN 2.7 ignores 'persist-key' and logs a warning about it on every start; the core export writes it regardless.

field.label: Add auth-nocache
field.help: Stops the client's warning about cached passwords on every reconnect. Pushed auth tokens are exempt, so silent renewal keeps working. Core only writes it for instances with an authentication source, which an SSO instance does not have.
